card.title: Ondal, Lending & Personal Banking
card.subtitle: A mobile banking experience combining fast lending with everyday banking for underserved UK consumers.

hero.title: Ondal, Lending & Personal Banking
hero.summary: A mobile banking experience combining fast lending with everyday banking for underserved UK consumers.

blocks.html:
Building on an existing payday lending business, the project expanded into personal banking for underserved UK consumers across two brands: Ondal and My Finance Club. The solution brings personal lending, repayments, multi-currency accounts, cards, and everyday banking into a shared product experience adapted to each brand.

Mid-project, a banking provider change required us to rethink payment and card flows, while the scope expanded to multiple currencies, accounts, and savings pots.

As Product Designer, I owned the end-to-end mobile experience across research, UX/UI design, prototyping, and validation. I designed key lending and banking journeys and worked closely with Engineering and Compliance to keep the experience simple, compliant, and technically feasible as the banking provider and product scope changed.

blocks.title: Business goals
items: Expand from payday lending into personal banking
Reduce friction across loan applications and repayments
Build trust with underserved banking customers
Deliver a compliant product ready for Beta

items.challenge: Unfamiliar with, or wary of, traditional banking and lending processes
Limited access to traditional banking and reliance on high-friction short-term lending

items.goal: Access funds again with minimal effort

blocks.html: Rather than treating lending and banking as separate products, I designed them as one connected customer journey.

blocks.title: We focused on two critical experiences:
items: Helping a first-time borrower transition into banking with minimal additional setup.
Making repeat borrowing faster for verified customers.

blocks.html: The initial app experience was designed for existing borrowers who had already completed KYC on the website. As multi-currency accounts and savings pots were added to the scope, the experience also needed to support growing banking complexity from the start.

items.finding: Returning borrowers had to re-enter the same information.
items.insight: Pre-filled applications for faster repeat borrowing.

items.finding: Repayment could be stressful and cumbersome.
items.insight: Flexible amounts and payment methods to make repayment easier.

items.finding: A new banking provider changed payment and card capabilities.
items.insight: Adapted key flows to the new API without disrupting the experience.

items.finding: The product expanded to multiple currencies, accounts, and savings pots.
items.insight: Created a scalable structure without adding navigation complexity.

blocks.html: Returning borrowers were repeatedly entering information we already had. I designed a streamlined reapplication flow with pre-filled details, letting users focus on the loan amount and terms before reviewing and signing.

Reducing repayment friction benefited both customers and the business. I designed quick-select amounts, flexible repayment values, and multiple payment methods to make paying back a loan as straightforward as possible.

As the product expanded into multiple currencies, accounts, and savings pots, the experience needed to grow without becoming harder to navigate. I designed a flexible account structure that kept balances, money pots, transactions, and common actions easy to access.

Because Ondal had not yet launched publicly, the impact of the work was measured through design validation and Beta readiness rather than post-launch business metrics.

Usability testing with 8 participants showed that the core lending and banking journeys could be completed with minimal friction.

items.label: Completed a loan repayment without assistance
Successfully navigated accounts, currencies, and Money Pots

blocks.html: Testing revealed orientation issues in sub-accounts, which were addressed before the Beta release.

The biggest lesson was designing for change.

The banking provider migration and expanding product scope pushed me to think beyond individual screens and design a flexible system that could adapt to changing technical and business requirements.

It also reinforced the importance of treating lending and banking as one connected experience, rather than adding banking features onto an existing loan product.

The next step after Beta would be to measure real customer behaviour and use those findings to refine the experience after launch.
